unit-m3u6.title: Unit 3 · Lesson 6: Multiply with Zeros
unit-m3u6.source: enVision Topic 3 textbook scan — Multiply Multi-Digit Whole Numbers (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 3-6 of the Topic 3 textbook scan: multiplying whole numbers when one of the factors has a zero in it.

why.text: Zeros cause more multiplication mistakes than any other digit — dropped, skipped, or forgotten when a carry lands on them.

objectives.text: Multiply whole numbers that have zeros in them
Add a carry into a place where the digit is 0

parentNote.text: The two slips this lesson targets are skipping a zero in the middle of a number (306 treated as 36) and forgetting that a carry can land on a zero (306 × 4 written as 1,204 instead of 1,224). Both are built into wrong options, computed in the builder. The textbook's own "Trudy doubles it" item is here with fresh numbers — it is really the placeholder-zero idea again, since the first 4 in 44 means 4 tens.

nextUp.text: Zero times anything is zero — but the carry still lands.

cards.def:
**A zero in a factor is multiplied like any other digit.**
• Any number × 0 = 0.
• You still write a digit in that place — the zero holds the place.
cards.hint: Zero times anything is zero, but it still gets its spot.

cards.term: A zero can still get a carry
cards.def:
**If something was carried into the zero's place, add it on.**
• 306 × 4: 4 × 6 = 24, carry 2. Then 4 × 0 = 0, plus 2 = 2.
• So the tens digit is 2, not 0: 306 × 4 = 1,224.
cards.hint: Zero × 4 is 0, but the carry still arrives.

cards.def:
**Dropping a zero from the middle of a number changes it completely.**
• 306 is not 36. 306 × 4 = 1,224, but 36 × 4 is only 144.
cards.hint: The zero is what makes 306 three hundred and six.

cards.def:
**If a factor ends in 0, you can multiply without it and put the zero back at the end.**
• 610 × 45 = 61 × 45 × 10 = 2,745 × 10 = 27,450.
cards.hint: Set the end zero aside, then give it back.

cards.def:
**An estimate catches a lost zero immediately.**
• 407 × 23 is about 400 × 20 = 8,000.
cards.hint: If the answer is about ten times too small, a zero went missing.

questions.q: To find 306 × 4, you first get 4 × 6 = 24 and carry 2. What digit goes in the tens place?
opts: 2, because 4 × 0 = 0 and the carried 2 is added
4, because the 4 in 24 goes in the tens place
questions.hint: What is 4 × 0? Then what do you add?
steps: The 2 tens carried from the ones get added.
0 + 2 = 2 tens, so the tens digit is 2.

ex.main: **2.** 4 × 0 = 0, and the carried 2 tens still have to be added.
ex.tip: Writing 0 there forgets the carry — that turns 1,224 into 1,204.

questions.hint: Multiply each digit, including the zero, and keep the carries.

ex.main: **1,224.** The zero place ends up holding the carried 2.
ex.tip: 144 is 36 × 4 — the zero in 306 was skipped.
Estimate: 400 × 23 = 9,200. 1,081 is 47 × 23 — the zero was skipped.
950 is 25 × 38 — it treats 205 as if the zero were not there.

questions.hint: Find 61 × 45, then put the zero from 610 back on.

ex.main: **27,450.** 61 × 45 = 2,745, and the end zero of 610 makes it 27,450.
ex.tip: Forgetting to put the zero back gives 2,745 — ten times too small.

questions.q: An auditorium has 108 rows with 26 seats in each row. How many seats is that?
questions.hint: Multiply rows by seats per row.

ex.tip: 468 is 18 × 26 — the zero in 108 got dropped.

questions.q: Trudy wants to find 44 × 404. She says she can find 4 × 404 and double it. Why does that not work?
opts: She should triple it instead, because 44 has two digits
Doubling works, but only when there is no zero in the numbers
44 is 40 + 4, not 4 + 4, so doubling only covers 8 groups
It does work — 4 × 404 doubled is the same as 44 × 404

ex.main: **44 is 40 + 4, not 4 + 4.** The correct product is 17,776; doubling only reaches 3,232.
ex.tip: The first 4 in 44 means 4 TENS — the same idea as the placeholder zero.

questions.q: Renting a trombone costs $36 a month. Buying one costs $475. Maria needs it for 12 months. What should she do?
opts: Buy it, because 12 months of renting costs $4,320
Buy it, because $475 is only one payment
Rent it, because $36 is less than $475
Rent it, because 12 months costs $432, which is less than $475
questions.hint: Find the total cost of renting for 12 months.
steps: $432 is less than $475, so renting is cheaper.

ex.main: **Rent it.** 12 months costs $432, which is $43 less than buying.
ex.tip: Comparing $36 to $475 on its own ignores the 12 months. $4,320 has one zero too many.

questions.q: Which estimate best checks that 309 × 42 = 12,978 is reasonable?
questions.hint: Round each factor to its greatest place.
steps: 12,978 is close to 12,000, so it is reasonable.

ex.main: **300 × 40 = 12,000.** It is close to 12,978, so the answer makes sense.
ex.tip: The other options each lose or add a zero when rounding.

steps: × 10 puts a zero on the end.

ex.tip: 1,060 is 53 × 20 — the zero in the middle of 503 was skipped.
